title: Chinese Rare-Earth Suppliers Quietly Halt Some US Shipments Ahead of Xi's September 24 Washington Visit
detail: A handful of Chinese rare-earth suppliers have refused to ship materials to US companies since early August, when Beijing sanctioned the Responsible Business Alliance (RBA), a US-based supply-chain due-diligence monitor, sources told Reuters in a report published September 4. The suppliers said they feared punishment from Beijing for complying with the RBA's due-diligence framework, even where the shipments themselves were otherwise licensed for export. The disruption has persisted for weeks and is now on the US planning agenda ahead of President Xi Jinping's September 24 visit to Washington. US officials have repeatedly pressed Beijing to honor rare-earth export-license commitments made in prior Busan and Beijing meetings, warning that renewed friction over critical minerals — used in defense systems, EV motors, and electronics — could overshadow preparations for the summit.

media.caption: Chinese rare-earth suppliers have quietly halted some shipments to US buyers since early August, weeks ahead of Xi Jinping's planned September 24 Washington visit

title: DeepSeek Orders at Least 160,000 Huawei Ascend 950DT Chips for New Inner Mongolia Data Center
detail: DeepSeek is preparing to install at least 160,000 Huawei Ascend 950DT AI accelerators at a new gigawatt-scale data center in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, Bloomberg reported September 4, citing people familiar with the plans — potentially one of the largest known clusters of Chinese-made AI chips assembled to date. The site, roughly 350km northwest of Beijing, was chosen for cheap wind and solar power and a 4.3°C average temperature that aids natural cooling; the facility is scheduled to partially come online in late 2027 or early 2028. The order underscores DeepSeek's continued pivot toward Huawei's domestic Ascend line for inference and post-training even as it still relies on Nvidia hardware for some training workloads. Fulfillment of the full order could take more than a year given Huawei's high-bandwidth-memory supply constraints on the 950DT, which is due to launch commercially in the fourth quarter of 2026.

media.caption: DeepSeek plans to install at least 160,000 Huawei Ascend 950DT chips at a new gigawatt-scale data center in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia
